claims.text: Real-time in situ characterization can identify time- and temperature-dependent oxide phase formation during high-temperature oxidation.
High-temperature environmental TEM or in situ XPS can reveal the kinetics and structure of oxide-scale formation.
Knowledge obtained through in situ characterization will allow researchers to design alloy modifications or coatings that produce more protective and adherent oxide scales.
Producing more protective and adherent oxide scales enhances oxidation resistance.
High-temperature alloy or refractory high-entropy-alloy surfaces can form non-protective oxides under oxidizing conditions.
Environmental TEM or in situ XPS can monitor oxide-scale growth dynamics during high-temperature oxidation.
Oxide-scale composition, uniformity, adherence, and growth kinetics mediate oxidation resistance.
Real-time observation enables identification of slow-growing, adherent oxide layers.
Alloy compositions or coatings enriched in Si, Cr, or Al can be tailored to promote formation of a protective oxide barrier.
A protective oxide barrier hinders further oxidation.
In situ monitoring will reveal conditions under which a more uniform and stable protective oxide layer forms.
Alloying or coating strategies guided by in situ monitoring will improve oxidation resistance relative to an untreated baseline.
Conventional high-temperature oxidation without guided optimization typically produces non-protective oxides that permit continued oxidation.
The approach is most applicable when oxide formation is primarily kinetically controlled and relevant transient phases can be captured in situ.
Mechanical stress or complex environmental chemistry may limit the applicability of results obtained through in situ oxidation measurements.
The quantitative oxidation-resistance improvement and scalability of the proposed approach across alloy systems remain unvalidated.
